title: S3 destination adapter with batching + checkpointing (SIEM-ready audit export)
creator: Diego Santos
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: SIEM-ready audit export (Beta)
content:
Goal
Implement the S3 delivery adapter for the audit-log-exporter service to support SIEM-ready audit export beta. This adapter is intended to be a “lowest common denominator” sink for customers who want durable delivery + later ingestion into their SIEM (or who already have S3-based log pipelines).

Scope (this ticket)
1) File format
- Emit newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) with one canonical Audit Event Schema v2 record per line.
- Optional gzip compression for cost/bandwidth (default: enabled).
- Each JSON object is the canonical audit event (no nested envelope). Do not include raw request/response bodies or other prohibited payloads per PII policy.
- Include exporter-added metadata fields only if they are part of the canonical schema or explicitly approved (e.g., export_destination_id and export_batch_id in a reserved namespace). If we add exporter metadata, document it.

2) Partitioning / object key naming
- Base prefix: s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/
- Partition by tenant/workspace and time to support efficient downstream processing.
- Proposed key shape (v1):
  <prefix>/tenant_id=<TENANT>/workspace_id=<WS>/date=<YYYY-MM-DD>/hour=<HH>/batch_<export_config_id>_<sequence>_<fromTs>_<toTs>.jsonl.gz
- fromTs/toTs are UTC timestamps (ISO-8601 compact) derived from the batch’s event timestamp range.
- Sequence is monotonic per (tenant_id, export_config_id) based on checkpoint state.

3) Batching
- Exporter hands adapter a batch of events already selected by checkpoint + filtering.
- Target bounds (configurable, with sane defaults):
  - max_events_per_object (default 5,000)
  - max_uncompressed_bytes_per_object (default 25 MiB)
  - max_flush_interval (default 60s) (enforced at exporter level; adapter just writes provided batch)
- Adapter must stream encode to avoid large in-memory buffers.

4) Retries + failure handling
- Adapter returns typed errors so exporter can apply retry/backoff policies.
- Ensure we distinguish:
  - retryable (transient AWS errors, throttling, 5xx)
  - non-retryable (access denied, invalid bucket/prefix, invalid KMS key)
- Surface enough context for operator troubleshooting but do not log secrets or customer identifiers beyond tenant_id/workspace_id and destination id.

5) Checkpoint integration
- Use exporter’s checkpoint interface: adapter is responsible for producing a deterministic “commit point” when upload succeeds.
- Success criteria: we only advance checkpoint after the object is durably written (PutObject success).
- At-least-once semantics: on retries/timeouts we may produce duplicate objects; downstream should dedup on event_id. We should minimize duplicates by using deterministic object keys for a given checkpoint range/sequence.

6) Server-side encryption
- Support SSE-S3 (AES256) by default.
- Allow SSE-KMS via configuration (kms_key_arn). If set, use aws:kms and the given key.
- For beta, assume bucket exists; do not create/modify buckets.

Non-scope
- Cross-account role assumption (unless trivial to include without blocking; otherwise track as follow-up).
- Multipart upload support > 5GiB objects (we will keep object sizes small via max bytes).
- Parquet/ORC output.
- Customer-managed partition templates.

Design notes / decisions
- JSONL chosen over Parquet for beta: easiest to validate, aligns with “generic S3 delivery” requirement, and avoids schema evolution friction early.
- Object key includes config id + sequence to simplify support triage (“which export config produced this file?”).
- Deterministic naming: sequence comes from checkpoint state to avoid unbounded duplicates when exporter restarts.
- Encryption: default SSE-S3. SSE-KMS gated by config and must be explicitly configured.

Acceptance criteria
- Given a valid S3 destination config, exporter writes audit events as JSONL(.gz) objects to the correct bucket/prefix.
- Objects are partitioned according to the key shape and include correct tenant/workspace + date/hour.
- Adapter uses SSE-S3 by default; SSE-KMS works when kms_key_arn is configured.
- Checkpoint advances only after successful upload; exporter resumes from the last committed checkpoint after restart.
- Adapter returns retryable vs non-retryable errors and is covered by unit tests.
- Integration test (localstack or AWS sandbox) validates:
  - object created
  - contents parse as JSONL
  - compression behavior
  - SSE headers set

References
- Canonical schema + SIEM mapping: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v2-and-siem-mapping.json
- Delivery semantics/idempotency ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-audit-export-delivery-semantics-and-idempotency.json
- S3 testing matrix: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/audit-export-s3-delivery-testing-matrix.json

Implementation plan (high level)
1) Define DestinationConfig model for S3 (bucket, prefix, region?, sse_mode, kms_key_arn, compression).
2) Implement encoder (streaming JSONL writer + optional gzip wrapper).
3) Implement object key builder (UTC date/hour derived from event timestamps; fall back to batch processing time if missing).
4) Implement upload via AWS SDK with correct headers and encryption params.
5) Integrate with exporter’s checkpoint commit flow.
6) Add unit tests + integration tests (localstack).

Rollout
- Behind feature flag (tenant allowlist) and destination type gating.
- Initial beta guidance: customers validate by wiring S3 to their existing log pipeline; Redwood does not guarantee exactly-once.

Open questions
- Should partition be by event timestamp or export time? (defaulting to event timestamp, but need to confirm behavior for backfill/replay.)
- Do we want a manifest file per hour/day for easier ingestion? (likely post-beta.)
comments: 2025-02-12 — Diego Santos: Drafted object key scheme (tenant/workspace/date/hour). Going with JSONL+gzip for beta. Will keep max object size low to avoid multipart complexity. Aligning with ADR on at-least-once + downstream dedup on event_id.

2025-02-14 — Marcus Lin: Reminder: no request/response bodies, no raw headers. Source IP and user agent only if present in canonical schema and already approved by PII policy. Please add a test that ensures we never serialize prohibited fields (e.g., prompt text).

2025-02-18 — Sean Gallagher: For operational visibility, please ensure adapter errors are typed and include destination id + tenant id, but no bucket policy contents / no credentials. Also ensure we expose upload duration + bytes in metrics (ENG-5168 will pick up).

2025-02-20 — Hanae Suzuki: SSE-S3 default is good. For SSE-KMS: require kms_key_arn and use aws:kms with the provided key. Document required KMS key policy expectations; customers frequently forget to grant decrypt/encrypt to the assumed role/user.

2025-02-25 — Diego Santos: Implemented adapter behind destination type s3 + feature flag check. Added localstack integration test for PutObject + gz decoding. Remaining: deterministic naming tied to checkpoint sequence (currently uses timestamp-based suffix; will adjust before merge).

2025-02-28 — Diego Santos: Updated object naming to use checkpoint sequence. This should reduce duplicates when exporter retries after timeouts (still at-least-once). Added unit tests for key builder and error mapping (AccessDenied => non-retryable).

2025-03-03 — Colin O'Donnell: Tested against a real S3 bucket in sandbox account using the testing matrix scenarios (SSE-S3 + bucket owner enforced). Looks good. Would be helpful to include example IAM snippet in docs; ok to defer to follow-up PR.

2025-03-05 — Diego Santos: Merged PR-1061. Creating follow-up to add SSE-KMS + cross-account assume role support (PR-1068) since multiple beta customers asked for customer-managed KMS and cross-account buckets.
